public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1187

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1187](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1187)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [GrTa08] Green, Ben and Tao, Terence, *The primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic
  progressions*. Ann. of Math. (2) (2008), 481-547.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos1187

/--
Let $k\geq 3$. Is it true that, in any finite colouring of the integers, there are monochromatic
arithmetic progressions of primes of length $k$?

It follows from the theorem of Green and Tao [GrTa08] (that any set of primes with positive
relative density contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions) that the answer to the first
question is yes for any $k\geq 3$.

See also [219](https://www.erdosproblems.com/219).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos1187.lean#L246"]
theorem erdos_1187.parts.i : answer(True) ↔ ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k →
    ∀ (κ : Type) [Finite κ] (c : ℤ → κ), ∃ S : Set ℤ, S.IsAPOfLength k ∧
      (∀ n ∈ S, ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ (p : ℤ) = n) ∧
        ∃ γ : κ, ∀ n ∈ S, c n = γ := by
  sorry

/--
Let $k\geq 3$. In any finite colouring of the integers, are there monochromatic arithmetic
progressions of length $k$ whose common difference is a prime?

The answer to the second question is trivially no: colouring the integers by their residue modulo
$4$ creates a colouring in which there is not even any monochromatic pair of integers whose
difference is a prime. Alternatively, one can just use $2$ colours and avoid any $3$-term
progressions whose difference is a prime by colouring $0,1\pmod{4}$ red and $2,3\pmod{4}$ blue.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos1187.lean#L246"]
theorem erdos_1187.parts.ii : answer(False) ↔ ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k →
    ∀ (κ : Type) [Finite κ] (c : ℤ → κ), ∃ (a : ℤ) (p : ℕ) (S : Set ℤ), p.Prime ∧
      S.IsAPOfLengthWith k a p ∧ ∃ γ : κ, ∀ n ∈ S, c n = γ := by
  sorry

end Erdos1187

reformulations.difference: The progression is represented by a set satisfying IsAPOfLength, whose underlying common difference is an unrestricted integer, rather than by an explicitly positive-step indexed progression.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For k ≥ 3, the definition's cardinality requirement excludes zero difference. A negative-step progression can be reversed by replacing (a,d) with (a+(k−1)d,−d), leaving its set of terms, primality, and monochromaticity unchanged. Conversely, a positive difference makes the k indexed terms distinct and satisfies the cardinality requirement. The full equivalence of the prime monochromatic progression witnesses was proved as Review1187.part_i_witness_iff in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean, using only standard axioms.

review.notes:
Both declarations faithfully express the two questions in Erdős's original survey: infinite hypergraph chromatic number means that every finite coloring has a monochromatic edge. Green–Tao Theorem 1.2 supplies part (i), and an independent Lean proof in /workspace/review/scratch.lean establishes part (ii) using residues modulo 4, uniformly for every k ≥ 2. Empty colors, empty/singleton progressions, prime boundary values, and the alternative two-color counterexample were also checked. The answer literals and solved tags are consistent with these resolutions and the mathematical status database.

The live erdosproblems.com pages returned Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive user-agent headers; the comparison therefore used the original cited papers and the status database. The exact linked external proof statements match the declarations; their transitive Green–Tao development was inspected at its entry points but not rebuilt.
